cancerguide_synt_1.white_male_private:
Patient Name: [De-identified]
MRN: [De-identified]
Date of Birth: [De-identified] Sex: Male Age: 68
Date of Visit: [Current Date]

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
68-year-old White non-, former smoker (35 pack-years), presents with newly diagnosed right upper lobe lung nodule. He is asymptomatic from a pulmonary standpoint and denies cough, dyspnea, or weight loss. There is no prior history of malignancy. He has a past medical history notable for hypertension and chronic pulmonary disease.

LUNG CANCER SUMMARY:
- Diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, grade 2, of the right upper lobe.
- Initial AJCC Stage (8th edition): Stage IA (T1a N0 M0)
- Tumor size: 14 mm (max dimension)
- No evidence of nodal involvement or distant metastasis.
- Clinical staging and imaging confirm a peripheral, early-stage lesion with no mediastinal node involvement.
- There are no separate pulmonary nodules or evidence of multiple lung cancers.

FUNCTIONAL STATUS:
- ECOG Performance Status: 1
- Karnofsky Performance Status: 90%
- Ambulatory with full range of motion, no reported activity limitations.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Patient identifies as White, male-identifying. He has a 30 pack-year smoking history and quit approximately 5 years ago. He is a retired engineer. Patient lives in a suburban community outside Hartford, CT. He is insured through private (Blue Cross Blue Shield PPO). No alcohol or illicit drug use reported. Lives independently.

PHYSICAL EXAM:
General: Well-appearing male, no acute distress.
Pulmonary: Breath sounds normal, no adventitious sounds.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender.
Extremities: No edema.
Neurologic: Alert, oriented, no deficits.

LABORATORY/DIAGNOSTICS:
- Imaging: CT and PET consistent with 1.4 cm right upper lobe part-solid nodule; no mediastinal or distant disease.
- Mediastinal nodes negative on imaging.
- No evidence of lymphovascular invasion.

SURGICAL EVALUATION:
- Patient is considered medically operable.

COMORBIDITIES:
- Hypertension, well-controlled.
- Mild chronic pulmonary disease.

VITAL STATUS:
- Alive

No evidence of advanced or metastatic disease at this time. No pertinent family history of lung cancer or other relevant malignancies. No relevant occupational exposures documented. 

[End of note]

History: 
66-year-old with a history of former tobacco use (18 pack-years), type 2 diabetes, and chronic pulmonary disease. She was recently diagnosed with a left upper lobe (LUL) pulmonary nodule.

Diagnostic workup: 
- Chest CT: 14 mm left upper lobe nodule 
- PET/CT: No evidence of nodal or distant metastases 
- No clinical evidence of separate pulmonary nodules or multiple lung primaries 
- Pulmonary function tests: [Not provided, but presumed adequate for operability per structured data] 
- Biopsy: Moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma (grade 2) 
- Biomarker testing: EGFR negative 
- AJCC 8th edition clinical stage: IA (T1a N0 M0), peripheral 
- ECOG performance status: 1 
- No relevant comorbidities precluding surgery

Case Discussion: 
The patient is a 66-year-old woman with clinical stage IA peripheral left upper lobe lung adenocarcinoma, without evidence of mediastinal lymph node involvement or distant metastases. She has no additional suspicious pulmonary nodules, and there is no evidence of multiple primary lung cancers.

Mediastinal staging is negative. Pulmonary reserve and performance status are sufficient for surgery. The patient is considered operable.

After multidisciplinary review, the consensus is that the patient has early-stage (IA, peripheral) non-small cell lung cancer, with negative mediastinal nodes and is a candidate for surgical resection.

No prior antineoplastic therapy, surgery, or radiation has been administered at this time. Patient remains alive with no interval from diagnosis.

cancerguide_synt_11.white_male_private:
[Deid: Name] is a 65-year-old with a history of former tobacco use (40 pack-years, now quit) who initially presented in 2022 with a right upper lobe lung mass. Diagnostic workup confirmed a moderately differentiated (grade 2) adenocarcinoma, measuring 45 mm, located in the right upper lobe. Staging was consistent with T3N1M0 (Stage IIIA, AJCC 8th edition), with no evidence of distant metastasis. 

On initial imaging, in addition to the primary lesion, there was a separate pulmonary nodule in the same lobe, without evidence of contralateral or extrathoracic disease. The patient's case was further characterized as a single primary tumor with separate nodularity, not multiple primary lung cancers. Mediastinal and hilar nodal evaluation did not identify N2 or N3 disease. 

The patient was deemed operable, and surgical intervention was pursued. Pathology following resection demonstrated R0 resection margins and nodal evaluation confirmed N0-N1 status. 

Performance status was ECOG 1 and Karnofsky 80%. Medical history is notable for chronic pulmonary disease (CCI 1), but no significant cardiac, vascular, or other major comorbidities.

No biomarker, molecular, or antineoplastic treatment data is available for this encounter. The patient is alive at the time of this note.

- Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm.
- Abdomen: Soft, non-tender.
- Extremities: No clubbing, cyanosis, or edema.
- Neurological: No focal deficits.

Comprehensive genomic testing performed (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, KRAS, MET, RET, NTRK, ERBB2, and PD-L1). Results: All actionable driver mutations negative. PD-L1 testing is pending.

Non-contributory for malignancy.

- Chronic pulmonary disease (COPD)
- No history of myocardial infarction, heart failure, cerebrovascular disease, diabetes, or additional major comorbidities
- No prior cancer or metastatic cancer
- No known immunodeficiency

- No documented thoracic surgical interventions
- No prior malignancy-related surgery

[Deid:Location] THORACIC ONCOLOGY CONSULT NOTE

Date of Encounter: [DATE]

Referring Provider: [Deid:Name]

Patient Name: [Deid:Name]
MRN: [PTID: SYN001]
Age: 67 years
Sex: Male
Race/Ethnicity: White, Non-Hispanic

REASON FOR CONSULT:
Evaluation of newly diagnosed right upper lobe lung adenocarcinoma.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
67-year-old male with a history of former tobacco use (25 pack-years; quit) presenting for evaluation of lung cancer. The patient was recently found to have a mass in the right upper lobe. Biopsy confirmed moderately differentiated (grade 2) adenocarcinoma. No evidence of multiple primary lung cancers or separate pulmonary nodules on imaging review. Staging workup, including imaging and clinical assessment, revealed a 32 mm right upper lobe lesion without evidence of regional lymph node involvement (N0) or distant metastatic disease (M0). Clinical stage at diagnosis is IB (AJCC 8th edition; T2aN0M0). The patient is alive and has no evidence of metastatic disease on current evaluation.

The patient reports a history of chronic pulmonary disease (COPD) but is otherwise functionally active with an ECOG performance status of 0 and Karnofsky score of 90. Charlson Comorbidity Index is 1, attributed to underlying lung disease.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
- Adenocarcinoma, right upper lobe lung (diagnosed 2023)
- Chronic pulmonary disease (COPD)
- No history of myocardial infarction, heart failure, cerebrovascular disease, diabetes, or additional major comorbidities
- No prior cancer or metastatic cancer
- No known immunodeficiency

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- No documented thoracic surgical interventions
- No prior malignancy-related surgery

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Patient is a former smoker with a 30 pack-year history, quit 5 years ago. No alcohol or illicit drug use. Lives independently.

ALLERGIES:
- No known drug allergies

CURRENT MEDICATIONS:
- None documented relevant to lung cancer treatment

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
- Pulmonary: No current cough, hemoptysis, or dyspnea limiting daily function
- Constitutional: No fevers, chills, or significant recent weight loss
- Cardiovascular: No chest pain or palpitations
- Neurologic: No focal deficits or headaches
- GI/GU/Other: Negative unless otherwise specified

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
General: Well-developed, well-nourished male in no acute distress
Lungs: Breath sounds normal, no adventitious sounds, no evidence of respiratory distress
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended
Extremities: No edema or clubbing
Lymphatics: No palpable lymphadenopathy
Neurologic: Alert, oriented, no focal findings
Other: No skin lesions

IMAGING/DIAGNOSTICS:
- CT Chest: 32 mm right upper lobe mass. No enlarged mediastinal or hilar lymph nodes. No evidence of metastatic disease.
- PET/CT: No hypermetabolic nodal or distant sites identified (N0, M0).
- Pathology: Moderately differentiated (grade 2) adenocarcinoma, right upper lobe.
- No molecular or PD-L1 biomarker results available at this time.

PERFORMANCE STATUS:
- ECOG 0
- Karnofsky 90

SUMMARY:
67-year-old man with clinical stage IB (right upper lobe, T2aN0M0, AJCC 8th) adenocarcinoma of the lung, in otherwise good health and considered operable. There is no radiographic or clinical suggestion of nodal involvement or metastatic disease. No evidence of multifocal or synchronous lung tumors. No previous anti-neoplastic therapy or surgical resection performed to date.

[Signature/Name], MD

Patient: [Deid: Name] MRN: SYNTH001 Date of Birth: [Deid: DOB] Sex: Male Age: 67

Subjective:
67-year-old male, former smoker (35 pack-years, quit), presents following a new diagnosis of right upper lobe non-small cell lung cancer (adenocarcinoma, grade 2), AJCC 8th edition clinical stage IVA (T2bN1M1b). He has a limited metastatic burden with a solitary metastasis to the left adrenal gland identified at diagnosis. Denies any other sites of disease.

He reports no significant respiratory symptoms today. Functional status is good; he remains active and is able to perform all activities of daily living. ECOG performance status is 1 (KPS 80). Past medical history includes diabetes and chronic pulmonary disease. No prior cancer-directed therapy initiated.

Review of Systems:
Negative for cough, dyspnea, chest pain, or constitutional symptoms. No neurologic changes or bone pain. Endocrine symptoms negative.

Medications:
No current antineoplastic therapy.

Social History:
Patient identifies as White, male-identifying. He has a 30 pack-year smoking history and quit approximately 5 years ago. He is a retired engineer. Patient lives in a suburban community outside Hartford, CT. He is insured through private (Blue Cross Blue Shield PPO). No alcohol or illicit drug use reported. Lives independently.

Family History:
Non-contributory.

Objective:
General: Well-appearing, alert, in no acute distress.
Vital Signs: BP [ ], HR [ ], Temp [ ], SpO2 [ ].
HEENT: Normocephalic, atraumatic.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm.
Pulmonary: Breath sounds clear bilaterally, no focal wheeze or crackles.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no organomegaly.
Extremities: No edema.
Neurologic: Alert and oriented, no focal deficits.

- CT chest/abdomen: 38 mm right upper lobe mass; right hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy consistent with N1 disease; solitary left adrenal mass, no other sites of metastasis.

- No evidence of lymphovascular invasion.

ECOG performance status 1.

67-year-old male with newly diagnosed right upper lobe lung adenocarcinoma, clinical stage IVA (T2bN1M1b) with a solitary left adrenal metastasis and good performance status (ECOG 1, KPS 80). PD-L1 40%. No prior therapy. Limited metastatic burden confirmed.

Smoking Status: Never smoker 
Comorbidities: Mild chronic pulmonary disease (CCI=1)

HPI: 
The patient is a 68-year-old who presented with an incidentally identified left upper lobe lung nodule. She has no history of tobacco use and no significant comorbidities except mild chronic pulmonary disease. She denies any symptoms.

Workup: 
Initial diagnostic chest CT revealed an 18 mm (1.8 cm) spiculated nodule in the left upper lobe, peripherally located, with no evidence of hilar or mediastinal lymphadenopathy. PET/CT was performed and did not demonstrate evidence of metastatic disease. Pulmonary function testing: FEV1 and DLCO are preserved. ECOG performance status is 0; KPS is 90.

A bronchoscopic biopsy of the lesion confirmed adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, with an EGFR exon 19 deletion. There was no evidence of lymphovascular invasion. Further staging classified the tumor as T1b N0 M0, AJCC 8th edition (clinical stage IA). No evidence of nodal or distant metastatic disease was found.

The patient was evaluated for surgical treatment and determined to be an appropriate operative candidate. She subsequently underwent surgical resection.

Pathology: 
Final pathologic evaluation of the resected specimen confirmed a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, 18 mm in greatest dimension, located in the left upper lobe. No lymph node involvement was identified (pN0). Margins were negative (R0 resection). No evidence of lymphovascular invasion.

Postoperative Course: 
The patient recovered without complication. Surveillance imaging was performed per protocol. She remains alive with no evidence of recurrence.

Primary Care Provider: [Deid: Name]

ECOG: 1 
Karnofsky: 90

Comorbidities: 
Charlson Comorbidity Index: 1, due to mild chronic pulmonary disease.

- Initial CT chest identified a 2.0 cm right upper lobe mass.
- Imaging workup included brain MRI (no intracranial metastases).
- PET/CT: No evidence of regional nodal or distant metastatic disease.
- Histology: Moderately differentiated (grade 2) adenocarcinoma.
- No suspicious mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
- Pulmonary function testing: FEV1 80% predicted; DLCO 110% predicted.

Social History: 
Patient identifies as White, male-identifying. He has a 30 pack-year smoking history and quit approximately 5 years ago. He is a retired engineer. Patient lives in a suburban community outside Hartford, CT. He is insured through private (Blue Cross Blue Shield PPO). No alcohol or illicit drug use reported. Lives independently.

Physical Examination: 
- Vitals: Stable.
- General: Alert, in no distress.
- Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation, no wheezing or crackles.
- No palpable lymphadenopathy. 

Labs: 
- CBC, Chemistry panel, LFTs within normal limits.

Educational Interventions: 
- Patient and family educated about diagnosis, surgical procedures, and perioperative expectations.
- Provided written materials regarding lung surgery.

Care Management Interventions: 
- Introduction to nurse navigator and lung cancer care team.
- Reviewed care coordination process and contact information provided.

Recent Results Reviewed: 
- CT chest, PET/CT, brain MRI, PFTs, pathology report.

cancerguide_synt_195.white_male_private:
[De-identified Name] is a 69-year-old with a history of former tobacco use (35 pack-years), who presented with a right upper lobe pulmonary mass. Imaging identified a 58 mm lesion in the right upper lobe, and biopsy confirmed moderately differentiated (grade 2) lung adenocarcinoma. AJCC 8th edition staging is T4 N1 M0, corresponding to clinical stage IIIA.

Past medical history is notable for cerebrovascular disease and chronic pulmonary disease; Charlson comorbidity index is 2. There is no history of diabetes, heart failure, renal, or liver disease. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a Karnofsky score of 90.

On further evaluation, staging studies confirmed locally advanced disease without evidence of distant metastasis. Lymphovascular invasion was present. There was no evidence of multiple synchronous primary lung cancers or separate pulmonary nodules.

Based on the tumor's involvement of the chest wall, the dominant anatomic issue was determined to be chest wall invasion. Patient proceeded with upfront surgical management. Surgical pathology revealed microscopic residual tumor at the margin (R1 resection).

The patient is currently alive. Vital status, laboratory studies, and comorbidities are as above. 

No assessment or plan documented at this time.

cancerguide_synt_200.white_male_private:
PULMONARY & THORACIC ONCOLOGY PROGRESS NOTE

Patient: [Deid: Name] 
MRN: [Deid: MRN] 
DOB/Age: 65-year-old male 
Race/Ethnicity: White, Not Hispanic or Latino

Chief Complaint 
Follow-up for lung cancer.

History of Present Illness
The patient is a 65-year-old male with a 30 pack-year history of tobacco use (now former smoker) and prior medical history significant for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. He was initially found to have a solitary pulmonary nodule in the right upper lobe on routine screening. He subsequently underwent diagnostic workup, which included CT imaging and PET scan. The CT revealed a right upper lobe mass, and PET demonstrated an FDG-avid lesion without evidence of mediastinal, hilar, or distant metastatic disease.

Bronchoscopic biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma histology. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided biopsy of mediastinal and hilar lymph nodes showed no evidence of nodal malignancy.

Preoperative pulmonary function tests were notable for mild obstruction, with FEV1 and FVC >65% predicted and DLCO mildly reduced but adequate for surgical consideration. ECOG performance status was 0, KPS 90.

The case was discussed in multidisciplinary tumor board, and the patient was considered a good surgical candidate based on functional and anatomic criteria.

Past Medical History

- Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
- Smoking (former, 30 pack-years)
- No history of heart disease, diabetes, or prior cancer

Social History

Patient identifies as White, male-identifying. He has a 30 pack-year smoking history and quit approximately 5 years ago. He is a retired engineer. Patient lives in a suburban community outside Hartford, CT. He is insured through private (Blue Cross Blue Shield PPO). No alcohol or illicit drug use reported. Lives independently.

Family History

- Not significant for lung or other relevant cancers

Review of Systems

At the time of pre-surgical evaluation, the patient denied chest pain, dyspnea, hemoptysis, fevers, weight loss, or other constitutional symptoms. Review of systems otherwise unremarkable.

Physical Exam

General: Well-appearing, no acute distress 
Vitals: BP within normal limits, SpO2 95-98% on room air 
Chest: Clear to auscultation, no wheezes, rales, or rhonchi 
Cardiac: Regular rhythm, no murmurs 
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender 
Extremities: No edema 
Performance status: ECOG 0

Laboratory and Imaging Summary

- CT chest: 33 mm right upper lobe mass, no mediastinal or hilar adenopathy
- PET/CT: FDG-avid right upper lobe lesion (SUVmax), no extrathoracic or nodal uptake
- Pulmonary function: FEV1 and FVC consistent with mild airflow limitation; DLCO mildly decreased
- Biopsy: Adenocarcinoma, grade 2, right upper lobe
- Mediastinal/hilar lymph node sampling: Negative for malignancy (N0)
- Biomarker testing: No actionable driver mutation detected (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF all negative); PD-L1 expression 5%
- No evidence of metastatic disease at diagnosis

Surgical Findings

The patient underwent right upper lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node dissection. Pathology revealed a 33 mm moderately differentiated (grade 2) adenocarcinoma, acinar pattern. All bronchial and vascular margins were negative for malignancy. Peribronchial and mediastinal lymph nodes (stations 2R, 4R, 7, 10R, 11R/L) were negative (0/number sampled). Lymphovascular invasion was absent.

Pathologic stage: pT2a pN0 M0 (AJCC 8th edition, Stage IB)

Postoperative Course

Postoperative recovery was uncomplicated. The patient maintained excellent performance status (ECOG 0) and returned to full daily activity. There were no major post-surgical or cardiopulmonary complications.

Follow-up

The patient was seen in oncology and pulmonary clinics postoperatively. He reported no respiratory complaints, chest pain, or constitutional symptoms. Serial surveillance imaging (chest CT and X-ray over the past year) has shown postsurgical changes without evidence of recurrence or new lesions. Pulmonary function tests remain stable, and patient continues to abstain from tobacco.

Current Medications

- Maintenance inhaler as needed for COPD
- No adjuvant systemic therapy

Allergies

- Penicillin G (rash)

Vitals (recent)

- BP: 138/84
- Pulse: 70
- SpO2: 97% on room air

Physical Exam (recent)

- General: Alert, no distress
- Lungs: Clear, postsurgical scar present
- Heart: Regular rate and rhythm
- No peripheral edema

Laboratory and Imaging (recent)

- CBC and chemistry panels within normal limits
- Recent CT chest: Mild restriction, postsurgical changes only; no evidence of recurrence

Summary

65-year-old male, former smoker with moderate COPD, diagnosed with right upper lobe stage IB (pT2aN0M0) adenocarcinoma. Negative margins, no nodal involvement, no driver mutation, low PD-L1 positivity. Recovered well post right upper lobectomy and mediastinal lymph node dissection. Maintains ECOG 0 performance status and in clinical remission on ongoing surveillance.

[Deid: Name] is a 67-year-old with a history of tobacco use (former smoker, 30 pack-years; quit 14-15 years ago), presenting with a diagnosis of right upper lobe lung adenocarcinoma. The diagnosis was established in 2023. Tumor histology is grade 2 adenocarcinoma. Initial staging per AJCC 8th edition is stage IIIA, with T4 (tumor size 51 mm, invasion of chest wall), N1, M0. There is evidence of lymphovascular invasion. Biomarker testing for EGFR/ALK/ROS1/BRAF/KRAS/PD-L1 is pending.

Comorbidities include chronic pulmonary disease (CCI = 1); there is no reported history of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular disease, or other significant comorbid conditions. ECOG performance status is 1, Karnofsky performance status is 80%. 

The patient underwent initial staging and evaluation, revealing a single primary right upper lobe lesion with no separate pulmonary nodules or multiple lung cancers. The primary tumor shows chest wall involvement, but no evidence of unresectability or distant metastatic disease. A chest wall evaluation was performed, and the patient proceeded with an upfront surgical approach.

Surgical management consisted of resection with negative margins (R0). No further surgery or concurrent induction therapy was indicated at this point. The postoperative course is notable for absence of margin positivity or unresectable residual disease.

At the time of this note, biomarker results are pending. The patient is alive and has not experienced disease progression or recurrence since initial diagnosis.

- Margins: R0 (negative) 
- Lymphovascular invasion: Absent

Patient ID: SYN001 
Age: 63 
Sex: Female 
Race: White 
Ethnicity: Not Hispanic or Latino 
Smoking History: Former smoker, 25 pack-years 
Comorbidities: Chronic pulmonary disease (CCI 1) 
Vital Status: Alive 

Chief Complaint: Newly diagnosed right upper lobe lung mass.

History of Present Illness: 
The patient is a 63-year-old former smoker (quit >15 years ago, 25 pack-years) who presented with an incidentally detected lung nodule in the right upper lobe. She has a history of chronic pulmonary disease but no other significant comorbidities.

Review of Systems: 
Constitutional: Negative. 
Respiratory: No new shortness of breath, cough, or chest pain reported. 
Other systems: Unremarkable.

Physical Exam: 
General: Alert and oriented, no acute distress. 
Lungs: Normal breath sounds, no wheezes or rales. 
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. 
Extremities: No edema or cyanosis. 
Other systems: WNL.

Diagnostic Studies: 
- Chest CT: 2.2 cm spiculated nodule in right upper lobe, highly suspicious for neoplasm. No significant mediastinal adenopathy. 
- PET/CT: Focal uptake correlating with right upper lobe mass, suspicious for malignancy. No hypermetabolic mediastinal or distant nodes. No evidence of extrathoracic metastatic disease. 
- Pulmonary Function Tests: FEV1, DLCO and oxygen saturation adequate for surgery. 
- Laboratory studies: Within normal limits.

Pathology: 
Diagnosis: Moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, grade 2. 
Location: Right upper lobe. 
Tumor size: 22 mm (2.2 cm). 
AJCC 8th edition pathologic stage: pT1b N0 M0 (Stage IA). 
Lymphovascular invasion: Absent.

Nodal Evaluation: 
Mediastinal lymph nodes negative for malignancy. No evidence of nodal metastases.

Operability: 
Patient deemed operable with good functional status (ECOG 0, KPS 90).

Surgical Management: 
The patient underwent curative-intent surgical resection. 
- Procedure: Anatomic right upper lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node dissection. 
- Margins: Negative (R0).

Postoperative Course: 
Uncomplicated recovery. Discharged in stable condition.

Summary: 
63-year-old woman, former smoker, with moderate chronic pulmonary disease, diagnosed with Stage IA (pT1bN0M0, grade 2) adenocarcinoma of the right upper lobe. PET/CT showed no evidence of nodal or distant metastasis. Surgical resection with negative margins was performed. Mediastinal lymph nodes negative. Patient has good postoperative functional status.

**Clinical Note**

Patient is a 66-year-old with a history of former tobacco use (45 pack-years, quit date not specified) who presents with newly diagnosed lung cancer. Histopathology confirms a moderately differentiated (grade 2) adenocarcinoma located in the right upper lobe. Initial diagnosis was established in 2021.

Staging workup per AJCC 8th edition reveals T2b primary tumor, N2 nodal involvement, and absence of distant metastasis (M0). Tumor size measured 46 mm. Lymphovascular invasion is present. Comorbidity assessment reveals a Charlson Comorbidity Index of 2, with additional history of cerebrovascular disease and chronic pulmonary disease.

On clinical evaluation, no evidence of multiple lung cancers or separate pulmonary nodules is found. ECOG performance status is 1, with a Karnofsky performance score of 90.

Mediastinal biopsy demonstrates nodal involvement at N2. No information is available regarding biomarker status. There is no evidence of metastatic disease or recurrence at baseline or initial staging interval.

The patient is alive and has not experienced disease progression or death at the time of this note.

Patient is a 68-year-old White non- with a former tobacco use history (25 pack-years) who was diagnosed in 2023 with right upper lobe lung adenocarcinoma, AJCC 8th edition stage IIIA (T1bN2M0), grade 2. At time of diagnosis, there were no separate pulmonary nodules or additional primary lung cancers. There was no clinical or imaging evidence of metastatic disease. ECOG performance status was 1 (KPS 90).

Initial diagnostic workup confirmed mediastinal nodal involvement (N2 disease) by biopsy. The patient did not have any N3 lymph nodes or distant metastases. Following pathologic confirmation of N2 adenocarcinoma, multidisciplinary discussion occurred and the patient was started on treatment with definitive concurrent chemoradiation as initial therapy. After completing chemoradiation, there has been no evidence of disease progression or recurrence on post-treatment evaluations.

Relevant comorbidities include chronic pulmonary disease and diabetes mellitus (Charlson Comorbidity Index: 2). The patient is alive with no evidence of disease progression based on most recent assessment.

After completing chemoradiation, there has been no evidence of disease progression or recurrence on post-treatment evaluations.

Relevant comorbidities include chronic pulmonary disease and diabetes mellitus (Charlson Comorbidity Index: 2). The patient is alive with no evidence of disease progression based on most recent assessment.

Clinical Note

Patient: SYNTHNSCLC01 
Age: 64 
Sex: Male 
Race/Ethnicity: White, Not Hispanic or Latino 
History: Former smoker, 25 pack-years

**Oncologic History:** 
The patient was diagnosed in 2023 with right upper lobe pulmonary adenocarcinoma (moderately differentiated, histology code 8140/3). At the time of diagnosis, AJCC 8th edition staging was T2b N0 M1b (Stage IVA). Initial metastatic sites include the left adrenal gland, detected at diagnosis.

**Biomarker Evaluation:** 
Comprehensive molecular profiling for EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, KRAS, RET, NTRK, MET, and PD-L1 was negative for actionable alterations. PD-L1 is negative.

**Comorbidities:** 
- Diabetes mellitus 
- Chronic pulmonary disease 
Charlson Comorbidity Index: 2

**Performance Status:** 
- ECOG: 1 
- KPS: 90

**Social History:** 
Former smoker (25 pack-years); no current tobacco use.

**Summary of Recent Findings:** 
- No evidence of additional primary tumors or separate pulmonary nodules.
- Limited metastatic disease burden is confirmed, with a single extra-thoracic metastatic site (left adrenal).
- Patient’s functional status remains good (ECOG 1).
- Thoracic definitive therapy (e.g., surgery or local radiation) is feasible and under consideration. 
- Tumor burden within the thorax fits T1-3 N2 or T4 N0-2 category.

**Additional Information:** 
- No prior systemic antineoplastic therapy or thoracic surgery reported at this time.
- No reported discontinuation or completion of prior lines of therapy.
- No mention of disease recurrence or progression outside current metastatic findings.

**Vital Status:** 
Alive, last contact 0 months from diagnosis.

**Relevant Prior Work-Up:** 
- No lymphovascular invasion noted.
- Tumor size: 45 mm.
- No biomarker-driven therapy is indicated based on present testing.

**Key Review Points:** 
- The patient is being evaluated for definitive local therapy to the thoracic disease, in the context of limited metastatic (M1b) involvement, good performance status, and absence of actionable biomarkers.

Evaluation and management of newly diagnosed right upper lobe lung adenocarcinoma.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS 
[Deid: Name] is a 65-year-old with no significant past medical comorbidities, who is a never-smoker, presenting for evaluation of newly diagnosed lung cancer. She was found to have a right upper lobe pulmonary nodule measuring approximately 20 mm. She denied cough, hemoptysis, chest pain, weight loss, or constitutional symptoms. There is no history of prior malignancy, and there are no significant comorbidities. She is independently functional (ECOG 0, KPS 90).

DIAGNOSTIC WORK-UP 
Pathology: 
- Biopsy of the right upper lobe lesion demonstrated moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma.
- EGFR molecular testing is positive for exon 19 deletion.

Staging: 
- AJCC 8th edition clinical stage IA (cT1bN0M0).
- Imaging (CT chest and PET/CT): Consistent with a 20 mm peripheral tumor in the right upper lobe. No thoracic or extrathoracic lymph node involvement. No evidence of distant metastatic disease.
- Mediastinal lymph nodes: Negative on imaging and/or sampling.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION 
General: Well-appearing female, in no distress. 
Lungs: Clear to auscultation, no focal findings. 
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm. 
No palpable lymphadenopathy.

SOCIAL HISTORY 
Patient identifies as White, male-identifying. He has a 30 pack-year smoking history and quit approximately 5 years ago. He is a retired engineer. Patient lives in a suburban community outside Hartford, CT. He is insured through private (Blue Cross Blue Shield PPO). No alcohol or illicit drug use reported. Lives independently.

PATHOLOGIC REVIEW 
- Moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, right upper lobe.
- Pathologic staging following surgery: pT1bN0M0 (stage IA).
- Margins negative (R0).

---

Patient Name: [Deid: Name]
Patient ID: SYNTHNSCLC001
Age: 68 Sex: Female Race: White Ethnicity: Not Hispanic or Latino

Date of Encounter: [DATE: 0]

Chief Complaint:
New diagnosis of right upper lobe pulmonary nodule.

History of Present Illness:
The patient is a 68-year-old former smoker (20 pack-years, quit) presenting for evaluation following the discovery of a right upper lobe lung nodule. She has a medical history notable for chronic pulmonary disease (COPD). She is asymptomatic from a pulmonary standpoint, with no cough, hemoptysis, dyspnea, chest pain, fatigue, or weight loss. No systemic symptoms reported.

Social History:
Patient identifies as White, male-identifying. He has a 30 pack-year smoking history and quit approximately 5 years ago. He is a retired engineer. Patient lives in a suburban community outside Hartford, CT. He is insured through private (Blue Cross Blue Shield PPO). No alcohol or illicit drug use reported. Lives independently.

Family History:
Non-contributory for lung cancer.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, fatigue, or weight loss.
Respiratory: Denies cough, hemoptysis, or shortness of breath.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain, palpitations, edema.
Other systems: Non-contributory.

Physical Exam:
General: Well developed, well nourished, no acute distress.
Vitals: Stable.
HEENT: Normocephalic, atraumatic.
Lungs: Breath sounds clear, normal respiratory effort, no adventitious sounds.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur, no edema.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender.
Neurological: Alert, oriented, no focal deficit.

Diagnostic Studies:
Imaging:
- Chest CT: 19 mm (1.9 cm) spiculated nodule, right upper lobe, peripheral location. No evidence of nodal enlargement or mediastinal adenopathy.
- PET/CT: Mild FDG uptake (SUV 2.3), no evidence of distant metastatic disease or abnormality elsewhere.
- Adrenal nodule identified; radiographically consistent with benign adenoma.

Biopsy:
- CT-guided percutaneous biopsy of the right upper lobe nodule: Histology shows moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, grade 2.

Pathology:
- Tumor size: 19 mm.
- Lymphovascular invasion: Negative.
- Surgical margin status: Not applicable (prior to surgery).
- No evidence of lymph node involvement (radiographically N0).
- No evidence of distant metastases (M0).

Staging:
- AJCC 8th edition: Clinical Stage IA (cT1bN0M0).
- Location: Right upper lobe, peripheral.

Performance Status:
- ECOG: 0 (fully active, no symptoms)
- Karnofsky: 90%

Comorbidities:
- COPD (Charlson = 1)
- No history of diabetes, CHF, MI, PVD, cerebrovascular disease, dementia, renal or liver disease, or other malignancy.

Medications:
- [Not specified in structured data]

Allergies:
- [Not specified in structured data]

Summary:
68-year-old woman, former smoker, presents with a 19 mm peripheral right upper lobe nodule with histologically confirmed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, no nodal or metastatic disease, excellent performance status, and no significant comorbidities to preclude surgery. Imaging and staging are complete with no evidence of mediastinal node involvement or distant metastatic disease. She is evaluated as a surgical candidate for presumed Stage IA peripheral NSCLC.

General: Well-appearing, alert, in no acute distress.

Diagnosis: Moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the right upper lobe.
Staging: AJCC 8th edition, clinical Stage IIB (T3 N0 M0).
 - Tumor size: 52 mm, chest wall invasion present (T3 by invasion).
 - No nodal involvement (N0) confirmed.
 - No metastatic disease (M0).
No evidence of separate pulmonary nodules or multiple primary lung cancers by imaging or clinical assessment.
No evidence of distant or mediastinal metastatic disease.

IMAGING/WORKUP:
- Imaging demonstrates a solitary right upper lobe lesion (52 mm) abutting or invading the chest wall.
- No mediastinal lymphadenopathy or distant metastases.

PERFORMANCE STATUS:
- ECOG 1
- KPS 90

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Patient identifies as White, male-identifying. He has a 30 pack-year smoking history and quit approximately 5 years ago. He is a retired engineer. After multidisciplinary discussion, the patient was considered a candidate for upfront surgical resection of the chest wall-invading right upper lobe lesion.

Pulmonary Oncology Consultation Note

Patient: [De-identified]
MRN: [De-identified]
Date of Visit: [De-identified]
Age: 68 years
Sex: Male
Ethnicity: Non-Hispanic White

Referral Diagnosis: Right upper lobe adenocarcinoma of the lung

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 68-year-old male with a significant prior smoking history (45 pack-years, now former smoker) who presented following abnormal chest imaging. Initial workup identified a primary tumor in the right upper lobe with additional nodules noted in the right lung. Subsequent CT imaging demonstrated a dominant lesion in the right upper lobe (measuring up to 4.8 cm) and multiple separate nodules in the ipsilateral (right) lung consistent with separate pulmonary nodules in the same lobe or ipsilateral non-primary lobe. PET scan confirmed hypermetabolic activity in the right upper lobe mass and associated nodules. Mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy was not enlarged by CT criteria.

Pathology from CT-guided core biopsy of the right upper lobe confirmed moderately differentiated (grade 2) adenocarcinoma (histology code 8140/3). There is evidence of lymphovascular invasion. No distant metastases were identified at the time of diagnosis. AJCC 8th edition clinical staging at presentation was stage IIIA (T3, N1, M0), corresponding to tumor with separate pulmonary nodules and ipsilateral nodal involvement.

The patient denies any constitutional symptoms such as weight loss or fevers. He reports stable activity tolerance. No significant respiratory complaints at present.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
- Hypertension 
- Hyperlipidemia
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus (no complications)
- Chronic pulmonary disease
- No history of myocardial infarction, congestive heart failure, peripheral vascular disease, cerebrovascular disease, peptic ulcer disease, moderate/severe liver disease, metastatic cancer, or AIDS

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Patient identifies as White, male-identifying. He has a 30 pack-year smoking history and quit approximately 5 years ago. He is a retired engineer. Patient lives in a suburban community outside Hartford, CT. He is insured through private (Blue Cross Blue Shield PPO). No alcohol or illicit drug use reported. Lives independently.

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Non-contributory

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
12-system review negative unless otherwise described above.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Vital Signs: Stable
Performance Status: ECOG 1 (Karnofsky 90)
General: Well-appearing male
HEENT: Normal
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender
Extremities: No edema
Neurologic: Non-focal

LABORATORIES:
No notable abnormalities.

IMAGING:
- CT Chest: Dominant right upper lobe mass measuring up to 4.8 cm; multiple ipsilateral pulmonary nodules; no pleural or pericardial effusion; no distant metastases seen.
- PET/CT: Hypermetabolic activity in right lung lesions as above.
- No evidence of contralateral or extrathoracic metastatic disease.

cancerguide_synt_317.white_male_private:
Chief Complaint

New patient referred for evaluation of lung cancer.

History of Present Illness

Mr. SYNTH001 is a 67-year-old with a significant smoking history of 50 pack-years (current or former smoker) who presents for further evaluation after a recent diagnosis of lung cancer. He reports a history of mild chronic obstructive pulmonary disease but denies any current or past congestive heart failure, diabetes, cardiovascular, vascular, or other significant comorbid conditions aside from his COPD (Charlson Comorbidity Index: 1, based on chronic pulmonary disease). His performance status is ECOG 1 (Karnofsky 80%), and he is currently alive with no evidence of dementia or neurological symptoms.

Diagnostic Summary

Pathologic and registry review confirm a moderately differentiated (grade 2) squamous cell carcinoma located in the right upper lobe of the lung. Tumor size measured at 29 mm on imaging. Initial diagnosis was established in 2023 (0 months since diagnosis).

Staging

Consultation Note

PATIENT NAME (MRN): [Deid: Name] ([Deid: MRN])
DATE OF SERVICE: [Deid: Date]

IDENTIFICATION 
[Deid: Name] is a 69-year-old , former smoker (40 pack-year history), with a past medical history significant for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He was diagnosed in 2023 with stage IA (T1bN0M0, AJCC 8th edition) adenocarcinoma located in the upper lobe of the lung. Tumor grade was moderately differentiated (G2). No evidence of lymphovascular invasion was present. There were no additional comorbidities except for COPD. ECOG performance status is 1; Karnofsky score is 90.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS 
The patient initially presented with an upper lobe lung nodule measuring 18 mm in greatest dimension, confirmed as adenocarcinoma on histopathology, and staged as T1bN0M0 by imaging and clinical evaluation. There has been no evidence of nodal or metastatic disease on the most recent workup. There is no evidence of multiple lung cancers or separate pulmonary nodules. Mediastinal nodes are negative. His smoking history is significant but he has since quit smoking.

The patient was evaluated for surgical resection, but was deemed medically inoperable due to underlying severe COPD and reduced pulmonary reserve.

PHYSICAL EXAM (most recent) 
General: Appears well, in no acute distress 
Lungs: Diminished breath sounds, consistent with underlying COPD; no rales or wheezing 
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs 
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended 
Extremities: No clubbing, cyanosis, or edema 
Neurological: Alert and oriented x3, no focal defects

LAB DATA (most recent) 
WBC: Within normal limits 
Hemoglobin: Stable 
Platelet count: Normal 
Renal function: Creatinine within normal limits 
Other routine labs unremarkable

IMAGING 
Chest CT: 18 mm upper lobe nodule, no evidence of nodal disease or distant metastases 
No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy identified 
No other suspicious pulmonary nodules

SOCIAL HISTORY 
Patient identifies as White, male-identifying. He has a 30 pack-year smoking history and quit approximately 5 years ago. He is a retired engineer. Patient lives in a suburban community outside Hartford, CT. He is insured through private (Blue Cross Blue Shield PPO). No alcohol or illicit drug use reported. Lives independently.

FOLLOW-UP 
The patient tolerated radiation therapy well. There were no significant acute toxicities. He was discharged home after completion of treatment. Surveillance with CT scan has been scheduled as per protocol. At last follow-up, the patient remains alive and well, with no evidence of locoregional or distant recurrence.

His smoking history is significant but he has since quit smoking.

The patient was evaluated for surgical resection, but was deemed medically inoperable due to underlying severe COPD and reduced pulmonary reserve.

General: Appears well, in no acute distress

Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs 
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended 
Extremities: No clubbing, cyanosis, or edema 
Neurological: Alert and oriented x3, no focal defects

LAB DATA (most recent) 
WBC: Within normal limits 
Hemoglobin: Stable 
Platelet count: Normal 
Renal function: Creatinine within normal limits 
Other routine labs unremarkable

IMAGING 
Chest CT: 18 mm upper lobe nodule, no evidence of nodal disease or distant metastases 
No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy identified 
No other suspicious pulmonary nodules

SOCIAL HISTORY 
Patient is a former smoker with a 30 pack-year history, quit 5 years ago. No alcohol or illicit drug use. Lives independently.

- Surgical margins: Negative (R0)
- All resected nodes: Negative for metastasis

- Mediastinal nodes: Negative by preoperative assessment
- Patient was deemed surgically operable

- No evidence of metastatic disease at diagnosis or at the time of surgery

Age: 65 y.o. 
Gender: Male 
Race: White

Reason for Visit: 
Initial evaluation for newly diagnosed lung cancer

History of Present Illness: 
The patient is a 65-year-old former smoker (40 pack-years, quit >15 years ago) presenting following abnormal imaging. He has a recent diagnosis of right upper lobe adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, measuring 32 mm (T2a). There is no regional nodal involvement (N0). Initial staging workup including PET/CT and brain imaging confirms a contralateral lung nodule, consistent with AJCC 8th edition Stage IVA (M1b, single metastatic site). There is no evidence of brain metastasis. No prior oncologic treatments have been initiated.

The patient denies significant comorbidities other than a history of chronic pulmonary disease and cerebrovascular disease (Charlson comorbidity index: 2). He is ECOG performance status 1, KPS 90, and functionally independent. There are no current or prior symptoms suggestive of CNS involvement. There is no history of prior thoracic surgery, radiation, or systemic therapy. He is currently alive with no recent hospitalizations for his lung cancer.

Social History: 
Patient identifies as White, male-identifying. He has a 30 pack-year smoking history and quit approximately 5 years ago. He is a retired engineer. Patient lives in a suburban community outside Hartford, CT. He is insured through private (Blue Cross Blue Shield PPO). No alcohol or illicit drug use reported. Lives independently.

Family History: 
Non-contributory for lung cancer

Review of Systems: 
Negative for cough, hemoptysis, chest pain, or neurologic symptoms.

Physical Exam (pertinent findings): 
- General: Well-appearing male, no acute distress
- Lungs: Breath sounds normal, no wheezing or rales
- No palpable lymphadenopathy
- No focal neurological deficit

Laboratory and Imaging: 
- Pathology: Right upper lobe, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, 32 mm
- Stage: T2a N0 M1b (contralateral lung nodule)
- Biomarker: PD-L1 expression 30%
- No evidence of liver, adrenal, bone, or brain metastases on staging
- No lymphovascular invasion documented

Clinical Course Summary: 
The patient presents with newly diagnosed right upper lobe lung adenocarcinoma (T2a N0) with a single metastatic lesion in the contralateral lung, consistent with AJCC 8th edition Stage IVA (M1b). He is ECOG 1, functionally independent, and fit for local therapy. The metastatic burden is limited (≤5 lesions, not involving brain). Thoracic definitive local therapy is technically feasible, and the disease burden includes N2 mediastinal involvement or T4 N0-2 disease as per imaging and staging data. No previous anticancer therapy has been administered.

CHIEF COMPLAINT 
Evaluation and management of newly diagnosed right upper lobe lung adenocarcinoma.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS 
The patient is a 67-year-old male with a significant history of tobacco use (30 pack-years, quit), chronic pulmonary disease, and diabetes. He was recently found to have a right upper lobe pulmonary mass. Initial evaluation and staging were performed in 2023.

PATHOLOGY AND STAGING 
Diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma, right upper lobe 
Histologic grade: 2 
Tumor size: 3.2 cm 
AJCC (8th edition) Staging: 
  • T2a N0 M0 
  • Stage IB (peripheral) 
No clinical or radiographic evidence of regional nodal involvement or distant metastatic disease.

CLINICAL COURSE AND WORK-UP 
The patient underwent complete diagnostic work-up. There are no synchronous or separate pulmonary nodules and no evidence of multiple primary lung cancers. Clinical evaluation did not reveal lymphadenopathy or extrathoracic spread.

Pulmonary function and comorbidity assessment confirmed the patient is operable.

SURGICAL CARE 
The patient underwent surgical resection of the right upper lobe lesion. Surgical margins were negative (R0 resection). Pathologic staging confirmed stage IB; there was no lymphovascular invasion.

POST-OPERATIVE STATUS 
He recovered well from surgery and follow-up examination revealed no evidence of residual or recurrent disease. Performance status remains excellent (ECOG 0).

SURVEILLANCE 
The patient will be monitored per standard post-operative surveillance protocols.

cancerguide_synt_387.white_male_private:
SUBJECTIVE:
[Deid: Name] is a 67-year-old with a history of adenocarcinoma of the left upper lobe (grade 2), initially diagnosed in 2024. He is a former smoker (30 pack-years). He presents for evaluation and management of his recently diagnosed non-small cell lung cancer. At presentation, he had symptoms related to his chest, but denies new or worsening complaints today.

He has no known distant metastases. There is no evidence of multiple primary lung cancers or separate pulmonary nodules on imaging.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
- Constitutional: No fever or weight loss reported.
- Respiratory: No hemoptysis or increased cough. Denies shortness of breath from baseline.
- Cardiovascular: No chest pain or palpitations.
- No other pertinent positives or negatives.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
- Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
- Chronic hypoxemic respiratory failure
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus
- No history of myocardial infarction, congestive heart failure, peripheral vascular disease, or cerebrovascular disease

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- No prior thoracic surgery

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Non-contributory for other thoracic malignancies

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Patient identifies as White, male-identifying. He has a 30 pack-year smoking history and quit approximately 5 years ago. He is a retired engineer. Patient lives in a suburban community outside Hartford, CT. He is insured through private (Blue Cross Blue Shield PPO). No alcohol or illicit drug use reported. Lives independently.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS:
- As per oncology and pulmonary comorbidities

ALLERGIES:
- No relevant drug allergies reported

OBJECTIVE:
VITALS:
- ECOG performance status: 1
- KPS: 90

PHYSICAL EXAM:
General: Well appearing, in no acute distress
Chest: Mildly reduced breath sounds at left upper lobe; no overt mass or chest wall abnormality on examination
No peripheral edema
No lymphadenopathy

IMAGING:
- CT chest: Revealed a mass in the left upper lobe with evidence of invasion into the chest wall (T4), measuring up to 4.5 cm. No separate pulmonary nodules or contralateral lesions. No evidence of distant metastases. Mediastinal and hilar lymph nodes not enlarged.
- No evidence of regional or distant metastasis (M0). 
- No evidence of pathologically positive mediastinal nodes.
- No other foci of intrathoracic disease.

LABORATORY:
- All pertinent labs within normal limits for staging and pre-treatment workup.

CLINICAL COURSE:
Patient has newly diagnosed, left upper lobe adenocarcinoma of the lung, staged as T4 N0 M0 (AJCC 8th edition clinical stage IIIA, with T4 extension into chest wall, but without nodal involvement or distant metastasis).

Case was reviewed for pre-treatment evaluation. There is no evidence of multiple synchronous lung primaries or separate pulmonary nodules. The dominant clinical problem is suspected chest wall invasion. No mediastinal nodal disease is present on staging. There are no findings to indicate unresectability at this time.

An induction therapy approach was chosen rather than upfront surgery, in accordance with standard care for suspected chest wall involvement without mediastinal nodal disease. After completion of induction therapy, the patient was reassessed and found to be a candidate for surgical resection (post-induction imaging confirms resectability). 

Patient is otherwise medically operable with good functional status (ECOG 1). All findings, history, and imaging have been reviewed with the patient and care team.

Clinical Note

Patient: [De-identified] MRN: [De-identified]
Age: 67 years Sex: Male Race: White Ethnicity: Not Hispanic or Latino

History of Present Illness:
67-year-old man with a 40 pack-year history of tobacco use (now former smoker) and a background history of chronic pulmonary disease, presented in 2023 with symptoms that prompted further evaluation. Imaging identified a right upper lobe lung mass; core needle biopsy of this lesion confirmed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma.

Staging work-up per AJCC 8th edition demonstrated:
- Tumor size: 38 mm (right upper lobe)
- Lymphovascular invasion: present
- Lymph node involvement: mediastinal and contralateral nodal disease (N3)
- No distant metastases (M0)

Clinical AJCC stage is IIIB (T2N3M0).

There is no evidence or history of multiple synchronous lung cancers or separate pulmonary nodules.

Biomarker analysis shows PD-L1 expression of 30%. No actionable driver mutations are documented.

Performance status at diagnosis: ECOG 1, KPS 80.

Comorbidity profile includes chronic pulmonary disease (CCI = 1); no history of myocardial infarction, congestive heart failure, cerebrovascular disease, diabetes, renal or hepatic dysfunction.

The patient is currently alive; there is no documented disease progression or death. 

No prior anti-neoplastic therapy, surgery, or radiation have been administered to date.

Laboratory and imaging data reviewed as above.

[End of clinical note.]
